result:
I've fixed search so it follows the live/archived rule for all four reports. It type-checks and all 617 existing tests pass. I didn't add any new tests.

- **Checks on every write** (`src/server/services/search-service.ts`): before adding an issue, comment or project to search, the code now checks it against the rule. Anything archived, or sitting under an archived issue or project, is removed from search instead. Comment entries are also tagged with their project now; before, that was left empty.
- **Archiving and restoring:**
  - Archiving an issue now also removes its comments from search (report 1).
  - Archiving a project re-checks the project, all its issues and their comments, so they drop out whether or not the issues were archived too. New comments and edits on kept issues stay hidden while the project is archived (report 2).
  - Restoring a project re-checks the same set. The project and its kept issues and comments come back; issues that were archived stay hidden, along with their comments (report 3).
- **Rebuild job** (`src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts`): it now pages through every project, issue and comment rather than stopping after the first 100 of each. That was why older content went missing in large workspaces. At the end it deletes any entry in that workspace's index whose item no longer exists, and it never touches other workspaces (report 4).
- **Comment edits** (`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`): editing a comment didn't update search before. It now triggers a re-index of that comment, and the re-index trigger handles comments and projects as well as issues.

Restoring an individual issue sends no event in this codebase, so it doesn't bring the issue back into search on its own. It only reappears after an edit or a rebuild. The rule doesn't cover that case, so I left it alone.
